disposition.defect: the R2 authority loader (scripts/v2a_authority_v2.py) checked freshness using bindings.reviewed_utc ONLY. Issue #163 requires stale INVENTORY to fail closed: the loader never required, never cross-checked, and never aged the physical inventory measurement timestamp (DISCOVERY-INVENTORY.measured_utc). A fresh review of a >72h-stale physical inventory measurement could therefore authorize a correctness-bearing campaign against a host that no longer matched the measurement. Additionally, the retained raw identity-probe bytes were bound to the structured proof only by self-reported structured digests, and the R2 zero-generation CPU control could pass through an unrelated duplicate-BDF rejection rather than the generation invariant itself
disposition.consequence: the R2 runs cannot establish the final discover -> review/freeze -> qualify contract for terminal purposes: the reviewed-discovery freshness gate did not age the underlying inventory measurement, so their PASS terminal is superseded pending R3 re-proof under the corrected contract

correction.inventory_freshness_contract: schemas inferswarm.v2a.discovery-inventory/3 and inferswarm.v2a.discovery-bindings/3 (scripts/v2a_discovery_v3.py) plus inferswarm.v2a.campaign-authority/3 (scripts/v2a_authority_v3.py): the loader requires and mechanically validates the inventory measurement timestamp itself (DISCOVERY-BINDINGS.inventory_measured_utc must exactly equal DISCOVERY-INVENTORY.measured_utc inside the digest-verified artifacts), parses all timestamps fail-closed (malformed, naive/non-timezone-aware, future, or inverted chronology rejected), enforces inventory measured <= binding reviewed <= authority/preflight freshness anchor, and enforces max_discovery_age_hours against the PHYSICAL inventory measurement, not merely the review event; a fresh review of a stale inventory rejects, and no caller-supplied enrichment can bypass it because the timestamps live inside the digest-verified artifacts
correction.raw_probe_provenance: one shared validation path (v2a_discovery_v3.validate_probe) derives the identity line, BDF, and zero-generation proof FROM retained raw stdout/stderr bytes and checks every structured field against that derivation; probe records carry explicit raw_stdout_path/raw_stderr_path; verification re-reads the retained bytes and re-derives: raw byte digest -> structured digest field -> selected-device identity/BDF -> zero-generation proof; tampering with raw stdout or stderr while keeping the structured binding unchanged fails closed; raw probe data stays NON_AUTHORIZING and NON_CORRECTNESS_BEARING and no correctness reference is derived from it
correction.zero_generation_control_repair: the R2 control test_probe_with_nonzero_generation_fails_closed could pass because its injected runner bound multiple twins to the same 02:00.0 BDF (duplicate-BDF rejection independent of the generation proof). The R3 controls (tests/test_v2a_discovery_authority_binding_r3.py) bind the twins to DISTINCT BDFs clean on every other axis and vary ONLY the generation evidence, injected and real probes exercise the same shared validation path, and the R2 probe evidence bytes are preserved unchanged
